title: UnCorrupt: Detection and prevention of Excel-style gene-symbol corruption in scientific spreadsheets
description:
Detects Excel auto-conversion damage in supplementary spreadsheets accompanying genomics papers: gene symbols converted to dates (SEPT7 -> Sep-07), RIKEN/accession IDs coerced to floats (2310009E13 -> 2.31E+19), leading zeros stripped, decimal-comma locale collisions, unicode homoglyph substitutions, time-coercion artifacts, and the rest of the Excel pathology documented by Ziemann et al. (2016, 2021) and Pyle (2017).

Validated end-to-end on three independent corpora:

  • Koh 2022 (full 7,945 supplementary files): 100% post-boost precision at user-facing thresholds, Wilson 95% [0.998, 1.000] on 1,630 xref-labeled cells.
  • Ziemann 2021 S2 (canonical paper ground truth): 98.78% cell-level recall (646/654).
  • Ziemann 2016 (independent paper, 2005-2015 time period): 100% recall on 279 validatable files, Wilson 95% [0.9864, 1.000].

Ships a Frictionless Table Schema sidecar (uncorrupt schema) that prevents future corruption: identifier columns pinned to type=string with regex constraints matching the inferred registry (HGNC, MGI, ZFIN, FlyBase, WormBase, rat). Any locale-aware re-import that coerces gene symbols to dates fails validation rather than silently corrupting.
references: Ziemann M, Eren Y, El-Osta A (2016). Gene name errors are widespread in the scientific literature. Genome Biology 17(1):177. doi:10.1186/s13059-016-1044-7
Abeysooriya M, Soria M, Kasu MS, Ziemann M (2021). Gene name errors: Lessons not learned. PLOS Computational Biology 17(7):e1008984. doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008984
Ziemann M, Poyet P, Lawson A (2023). The five pillars of computational reproducibility: bioinformatics and beyond. Briefings in Bioinformatics 24(6):bbad375. doi:10.1093/bib/bbad375
Koh JLY (2022). Gene Updater: a Web tool that autocorrects and updates for Excel misidentified gene names. Scientific Reports 12(1):14002. doi:10.1038/s41598-022-17104-3
Pyle JR (2017). Escape Excel: a tool for preventing gene symbol and accession conversion errors. PLOS ONE 12(9):e0185207. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0185207
